title: External attestors are trusted by design; calibrate, don't gate
description:
TRUSTING EXTERNAL ATTESTORS IS FUNDAMENTAL, NOT A HAZARD TO BE MINIMISED. Mark,
2026-09-15. hired is a trust aggregator by construction: its entire purpose is
to put many human-identity authorities behind one socket. An authority it
refuses to trust is an identity source it does not support.

IT ALREADY DOES THIS, ON EVERY REQUEST. The "compiled-in Rust attestor" is a
CLIENT SHIM, not an authority. The authority is always somewhere else:

  ssh.rs        speaks the SSH agent wire protocol over SSH_AUTH_SOCK (:3, :70)
                -- another process, holding keys hired never sees
  gpg.rs        tokio::process::Command spawns the gpg binary (:139-147)
  tailscale.rs  raw HTTP/1.1 to tailscaled's LocalAPI over its Unix socket
  unix.rs       getpwuid_r, whose own doc comment at :20 notes a directory
                backend may answer -- see persona-ouo5.5, that can be NSS over
                the network

So there is no in-process/out-of-process boundary to defend. A 2028-class
biometric sensor in its own box (see persona-3tly epic notes) is the same
architecture as ssh-agent, at a higher tier and over a longer wire.

THIS IS THE SAME MISTAKE SHAPE AS THE NO-NETWORK POSTURE, already made and
already reversed -- see the personad-may-use-the-network memory, commits
5edfbb6 and its revert. "Refusing the network does not make those sources
local, it makes them unsupported." Refusing external attestors does not make
identity local; it makes it absent. Do not re-propose either.

SO THE QUESTION IS NOT WHETHER, IT IS WITH WHAT CALIBRATION. Trust here is
graduated and explicit, never binary. What the daemon needs, and does not have:

  ENROLMENT       being able to connect must not be sufficient to be believed.
                  ssh-agent is trusted because SSH_AUTH_SOCK is in the user's
                  own session -- an inherited ambient decision that does not
                  generalise to a box on the network. An external attestor
                  needs a decision recorded somewhere, the way persona's GPG
                  enrolment rule is recorded (see gpg-key-validity-policy).

  PER-CONNECTION  peer credentials and, where available, LSM context -- at
  ATTESTATION     least what persona-5s4b.117 wants for consumers. Note the
                  asymmetry that sets the bar: a mis-attested CONSUMER receives
                  a credential it should not have, bounded by its own
                  pseudonym. A mis-attested ATTESTOR mints assurance for an
                  identity nothing established, for every consumer at once.
                  Same mechanism, strictly more consequence.

  TIER CEILING    what a given attestor is permitted to assert. This is the
                  calibration that makes trusting external sources SAFE rather
                  than merely necessary: a sensor class that can establish
                  hardware-bound biometric presence may assert it; one that
                  cannot must not be able to claim it by saying so. Without a
                  ceiling, trust is all-or-nothing and the only safe answer
                  becomes refusal -- which is the posture this bead rejects.

  UNATTESTABLE    present but unattestable is a refusal, consistent with the
                  fail-shut default at hire-grpc/src/service.rs:238-247. Note
                  this is a refusal of THAT SOURCE, not of the request: hired
                  still issues from whatever else proved.

RELATIONSHIP TO persona-5s4b.8: that bead covers registration and availability
probing -- a packaging question. This is the authorization question underneath
it. They should land together; a registration path with no calibration story
would make every registered attestor equally believed, which is the failure
mode this bead exists to prevent.
acceptance_criteria: A written trust model: how an external attestor is enrolled, how it is attested per connection, what tier ceiling it carries, and what happens when attestation fails. The model must ADMIT new external authorities, not merely restrict them.
notes:
TIER CEILING: DO NOT INVENT THE GRADING, added 2026-09-15.

The description above leaves 'what tier may this attestor assert' as a local
judgment call. For biometric attestors it does not have to be. External
standards already grade exactly this, and the ceiling should be pinned to one
rather than to our opinion of a device.

WHAT THE STANDARD IS AND IS NOT. ISO/IEC 30107-3 is 'Biometric presentation
attack detection -- Part 3: Testing and reporting'. It is REQUIREMENTS AND
METRICS, NOT A PROTOCOL: it defines how a lab evaluates a PAD subsystem and how
the result is expressed -- APCER (attack presentations misclassified as bona
fide), BPCER (bona fide presentations rejected), against a stated attack
potential. It says nothing about how a sensor conveys anything at runtime. In
the same family, Part 1 is framework and vocabulary and Part 2 is data formats
(CBEFF-oriented structures for carrying PAD results) -- and even Part 2 is an
encoding, not a protocol. There is nothing here to 'speak'.

SO THE CEILING IS AN ENROLMENT-TIME FACT, NOT A RUNTIME ASSERTION. This is the
right shape and it is a CONSTRAINT rather than a MECHANISM: do not ask a sensor
at connect time what it is certified for and believe it. Record the
certification when the attestor is enrolled, derive its permitted tier from that
once, and let the runtime path carry no negotiation at all. A compromised sensor
then cannot talk its way up, because there is no channel by which anything could.
This composes with the enrolment requirement already in the description -- being
able to connect must not be sufficient to be believed -- and makes it concrete:
what enrolment RECORDS is the grading.

FOR A MACHINE-READABLE SOURCE rather than a PDF certificate, the existing
artifact is FIDO's Metadata Service: signed per-authenticator metadata keyed by
AAGUID, carrying certification status including biometric component
certification. 30107-3 is the criteria a lab tests against to populate that.
CONFIDENCE NOTE: the 30107 structure above is stated with confidence; exactly
which certification fields MDS exposes today is less certain and was not
verified. Check before building against it.

NOTE THE FIT WITH persona-personad-may-use-the-network: consuming MDS is an
HTTPS fetch of signed metadata, which is the same shape as did:web and OIDC
JWKS and is already settled as permitted.
